newsitem.title: CHINA: Yuan closes down against U.S. dollar in Shanghai.
newsitem.headline: Yuan closes down against U.S. dollar in Shanghai.

text.p: The Chinese yuan moved down on a technical correction to close at 8.2972 against the U.S. dollar in Shanghai on Friday from its 20-month high of 8.2945 on Thursday, traders said.
Dealers said the fall was a temporary correction to the yuan's general upward trend.
The yuan opened lower at 8.2948 and consolidated down for most of the session, hitting an intraday high of 8.2906 and an intraday low of 8.2974 before closing.
Trading was dull with most done at 8.2958, traders said.
One dealer said that the extent of central bank intervention in the market today was unclear, but the yuan's failure to move beyond yesterday's high price increased selling on the topside.
"The yuan faced greater selling pressure at about 8.2950," he added.
But a second dealer said that the yuan's fall today was excessive given the underlying pro-yuan market sentiment.
"There is firm support at the bottom at about 8.2980 which will be difficult to breach," he said.
They expected the yuan would move around 8.2960 next Monday.
The yuan closed little changed at 7.0950 from 7.0931 against 100 Japanese yen and down at 1.0726 from 1.0715 against the Hong Kong dollar.
